channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: US ground stop: Saturday ends with about 6,400 cancellations; more than 900 Sunday flights already cancelled
item.description: Sunday, 15 Nov · Reuters, citing the flight tracker FlightAware, reports that Saturday ended with more than 6,400 US flights cancelled and more than 8,000 delayed, according to Latin Times. ABC7 puts Saturday's cancellations at nearly 6,500. By late Saturday US time, about 910 flights scheduled for Sunday had already been cancelled, both outlets report. The FAA reports no active ground stops. FAA chief Bryan Bedford has said he expects "full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday".

item.title: Delhi air: Sunday morning: still 'very poor', smog over the city
item.description: 15 Nov 2026 · Delhi's AQI is 351 at 8 am, per CPCB data reported by Business Today, still in the 'very poor' band and about the same as Saturday morning. Several stations are in the 'severe' band (above 400), with IIT Delhi the worst at 426. PM2.5, the fine dust that gets deep into the lungs, is the main pollutant at most stations. No rain had been reported by Sunday morning. Stage III curbs stay in place.

item.title: US ground stop: Duffy blames contractor L3Harris; FAA finds "zero evidence of anything nefarious"
item.description: Saturday, 14 Nov (US daytime; evening IST) · At a Saturday briefing, Duffy says the outage began while the contractor L3Harris, which runs the FAA's telecoms network, was switching lines from copper to fibre at a remote FAA site, and a router "started flooding other routers". He says officials are checking "whether we had incompetence" by the contractor or a faulty router, and that "We're going to hold people accountable." FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford says officials found "zero evidence of anything nefarious and zero evidence of anything AI related", and that the review will show whether the router was installed or set up wrongly, or was faulty. The FAA has switched off the problem function on about 60 routers of the same type. L3Harris says it is supporting the FAA's investigation. CBS News, citing senior government sources, says the problem was isolated to old Cisco routers.

item.title: US ground stop: Saturday cancellations pass 5,000; full recovery expected by Sunday night
item.description: Saturday, 14 Nov (1:18 am IST 15 Nov count) · FlightAware counts more than 5,000 US flights cancelled on Saturday by 2:48 pm US Eastern time (1:18 am IST Sunday), including 892 at American, 734 at Delta and 733 at United. Bedford says "the worst is behind us" and that airlines expect to have their full schedules running by the close of business on Sunday. About 130 Sunday flights had been cancelled by Saturday afternoon. Bedford says passengers will either be put on another flight or get a full refund; airline waivers generally do not cover hotels and meals.

item.title: US ground stop: Controllers' union: contact with some planes was disrupted; Congress to review
item.description: Saturday, 14 Nov · Nick Daniels, president of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, tells Yahoo News that communications with some planes were disrupted and controllers moved flights to working radio frequencies. On Duffy's criticism of L3Harris he says: "I don't think blame changes anything. Action changes things." The leaders of the House transport committee say they will "thoroughly review" what led to the stop, and Senate Commerce Committee Democrat Maria Cantwell says her committee will review it. New York Governor Kathy Hochul calls on Duffy to resign. Bedford says finishing the upgrade of the air traffic control system needs about $10.1 billion more, and Duffy plans to send Congress a new funding request on Monday.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Who might replace Huang: Trump backs Tim Cook; other names floated
item.description: 14 Nov 2026 · On Thursday, hours after the resignation, President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that "there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple." Nvidia and Apple had not replied to requests for comment, per Newsweek. Business Insider reports that the Financial Times said Nvidia had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, though it is not certain he would be offered the job or accept it, and that a person familiar with the matter told Semafor Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji is being considered. Analysts have also named Nvidia's Ian Buck and interim CEO Colette Kress. Nvidia has not named any candidates.

item.title: SpiceJet: Stock exchange warns of a trading halt; SpiceJet promises results by 7 December
item.description: 13 Nov · The BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange) says in a notice issued on Monday that it will suspend trading in SpiceJet shares from 10 December, because the airline has not filed its results for the March and June 2026 quarters. The suspension will not happen if SpiceJet meets the listing rules by 7 December. On Friday SpiceJet says it will publish the overdue results by that deadline. A spokesperson tells Reuters: "The completion of audit has taken longer time and hence caused delay in filing of results." SpiceJet's last results, published in February, covered October to December 2025.

item.title: Air India 171: Draft to be filed in a sealed cover in October
item.description: 28 Jul 2026 · The Solicitor General tells the Supreme Court that the draft final report will be filed in a sealed cover in the first week of October, and that four simulator tests sought by a petitioner have been done. The court says the pilots' federation can send its inputs to the AAIB and lists the case for 13 October.

item.title: Air India 171: AAIB to Supreme Court: draft report around October
item.description: 14–15 Jul 2026 · In an affidavit, the AAIB says it has completed 49 of 66 required investigation steps, that remaining work should take about six weeks, and that a draft final report is expected around October 2026. Analysis of engine monitoring data and of organisational factors is still under way. The draft must first go to the US National Transportation Safety Board for comments. The AAIB argues a court-monitored inquiry is not needed because its investigation follows international rules and is about safety, not blame.

item.title: Air India 171: One year on: "significant progress", no date for the report
item.description: 11 Jun 2026 · On the eve of the first anniversary, the AAIB says it has made significant progress analysing aircraft systems, flight recorder data, engine parts and maintenance records, but gives no timeline. The final report will come only after international review under ICAO rules. Four days later, Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu says the report is expected soon.

item.title: Air India 171: Supreme Court: "no suggestion of fault" in the report
item.description: 7 Nov 2025 · Hearing a petition by the father of the flight's captain and the Federation of Indian Pilots, who seek an independent, court-monitored inquiry, the bench says the preliminary report contains "no insinuation" against the pilot. When the petitioners cite a Wall Street Journal report quoting an unnamed source, the court says it is "not bothered by foreign reports". It issues notices to the government, the DGCA and the AAIB.

item.title: Air India 171: Air India: no problems found with switch locks
item.description: 22 Jul 2025 · Air India says its checks of the fuel switch locking mechanisms on its Boeing planes found no problems.

item.title: Air India 171: Investigators ask the public not to speculate
item.description: 17 Jul 2025 · The AAIB appeals to the media and the public to avoid speculation and wait for the final report.

item.title: Air India 171: FAA: fuel switch design is not unsafe
item.description: 11–14 Jul 2025 · In a notice to other countries' regulators dated 11 July, the US Federal Aviation Administration says the fuel switch design, including its lock, is not an unsafe condition that would require an airworthiness directive on any Boeing model, including the 787. Boeing refers questions to the FAA notice.

item.title: Air India 171: Preliminary report: both fuel switches moved to CUTOFF
item.description: 12 Jul 2025 (early hours IST) · The AAIB's 15-page preliminary report says that about three seconds after lift-off, the fuel control switches for both engines moved from RUN to CUTOFF, one second apart, starving the engines of fuel. They were moved back to RUN about 10 and 14 seconds later and one engine began to relight, but the plane was too low to recover. On the cockpit recording, one pilot asks the other, "Why did you cut off?" and the other says he did not; the report does not say who said what. It finds the plane airworthy, notes that Air India had not done a 2018 FAA-advised check of the switch locks because it was not mandatory, and makes no safety recommendations.

item.title: Air India 171: All 260 victims identified
item.description: 28 Jun 2025 · Authorities finish identifying the victims, mostly through DNA tests.

item.title: Air India 171: Flight recorders recovered and read in Delhi
item.description: 13–24 Jun 2025 · The first flight recorder is found on 13 June and the second on 16 June. The DGCA orders extra checks on Air India's Boeing 787 fleet from 15 June. On 24 June, data from the front recorder is downloaded at the AAIB's lab in Delhi; the rear one is too damaged for standard recovery.

item.title: Air India 171: Flight 171 crashes seconds after take-off
item.description: 1:38 pm IST, 12 Jun 2025 · The Boeing 787-8, bound for London Gatwick, crashes about 32 seconds after taking off from Ahmedabad and hits the campus of BJ Medical College. 241 of the 242 people on board die, including all 12 crew, along with 19 people on the ground; one passenger survives. Former Gujarat chief minister Vijay Rupani is among the victims. The Tata Group, which owns Air India, announces a voluntary payment to each victim's family.

item.title: US ground stop: FAA stops all departures across the US
item.description: 2:24 am IST, 14 Nov · Just before 4 pm US Eastern time on Friday, the FAA orders a ground stop for all US airports after "communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers", which guide planes at high altitude between airports. Planes already in the air keep flying to their destinations. Some flights over the ocean and from Alaska and Hawaii are allowed to leave.

item.title: US ground stop: Officials: a telecommunications outage, not an attack
item.description: Early hours IST, 14 Nov · The FAA says the problem is not a cyber attack. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin calls it "a telecommunication outage" and says all flights are accounted for. Airlines pause new departures and cancellations start to climb.

item.title: US ground stop: Ground stop lifted after about four hours
item.description: 6:45 am IST, 14 Nov · The FAA lifts the stop at 8:15 pm US Eastern time. It says it tested its systems first to make sure they were stable. Delta and United say they are resuming flights, but airlines warn that delays and cancellations will continue into the weekend.

item.title: US ground stop: Duffy blames old equipment: "It got overloaded"
item.description: ≈ 7 am IST, 14 Nov · At a late-night press conference, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says old switches and routers that carry air traffic data were overloaded and began giving inconsistent data. Mullin says new security patches added to the older system appear to have overwhelmed the routers, and that the outage is not linked to the Microsoft outage a day earlier. Duffy warns there will be more such outages unless the system is upgraded and calls for funding, saying "This is an emergency."

item.title: US ground stop: More than 3,400 Saturday flights cancelled as airlines recover
item.description: Saturday, 14 Nov (5:15 pm IST count) · FlightAware counts more than 3,400 flights within, into or out of the US cancelled by Saturday morning (6:45 am US Eastern, 5:15 pm IST), as planes and crews are out of place after Friday's stop. Delta has cancelled 629 flights, about 20% of its schedule, and JetBlue 335, about 40%. Delta is letting passengers change Friday and Saturday flights without extra cost; United is waiving change fees for travel between 12 and 20 November. Officials say the system should be working normally in time for Thanksgiving travel later this month.

item.title: Flying this winter: US flights halted for four hours
item.description: 14 Nov · A nationwide ground stop in the US, from 2:24 am to 6:45 am India time, cancels thousands of flights. Travellers flying to or from the US this weekend should check their connections. See the full timeline of the US ground stop.

item.title: Delhi air: Back to 'very poor'; light rain possible on Sunday
item.description: 14 Nov 2026 · Delhi's AQI eases to 349 at 7 am, back in the 'very poor' band after a day of 'severe' air. Some stations are still 'severe', including IIT Delhi at 419. The weather office (IMD) says a western disturbance could bring very light rain or drizzle to parts of Delhi on Sunday, with stronger winds that may help clear the air. Stage III curbs stay in place.

item.title: SpiceJet: Board to consider raising money
item.description: 13 Nov · SpiceJet tells the stock exchanges that its board will meet on 18 November to consider raising fresh capital through shares, preference shares, debt or a share sale to institutional investors.

item.title: Delhi air: NCR schools go hybrid; severe air forecast to last
item.description: 13 Nov 2026 · Noida, Greater Noida and Ghaziabad move classes up to grade 5 to hybrid mode, and Ghaziabad halts government and private construction until 20 November. The weather office (IMD) expects air to stay 'very poor' to 'severe' until 16 November. Stage III curbs remain; no move to Stage IV had been announced.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Market value falls below $4 trillion
item.description: 13 Nov 2026 · Nvidia shares fall 2% to close at $162.85, ending the week down about 12%, and its market value closes below $4 trillion. It was worth as much as $5.75 trillion on 5 October. HSBC downgrades the stock to Hold and cuts its price target to $170 from $365, a day after Bernstein cut its target to $200 from $400.

item.title: AI this week: ChatGPT agents can now pay for things
item.description: 13 Nov 2026 · OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for US Pro users, letting its agents make purchases with card networks' tokens after the user approves each one.

item.title: AI this week: Anthropic IPO reportedly six times oversubscribed
item.description: 12–13 Nov 2026 · Bloomberg News reports demand for Anthropic's shares at about six times the shares on offer, ahead of pricing expected on 18 November.

item.title: OpenAI: ChatGPT Wallet and security agents
item.description: 12–13 Nov 2026 · OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, which lets its 'dots' AI agents buy things for users, with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. It is limited at first to ChatGPT Pro users aged 18 or over in the US, who approve each purchase with a check such as Face ID; it will not work on sites that block agents. A day earlier, President Greg Brockman showed Daybreak Red Team, in early access, which uses AI agents to test web apps for security holes, and Daybreak Defense Factory, which prepares fixes for engineers to review.

item.title: Anthropic: IPO reportedly six times oversubscribed
item.description: 12–13 Nov 2026 · Bloomberg News reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that the share sale has drawn about six times as many orders as there are shares, and that bankers will favour existing backers, so some buyers may get less than expected. At the top of the range the sale would raise up to $64.4 billion. Demand figures could still change; Anthropic had not commented.

item.title: Outlook outage: Microsoft names a cause and apologises
item.description: 13 Nov 2026 · In an updated statement, Microsoft says the incident "was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change", and that it was a technical issue not related to cyber attacks or AI agents. It says it is "deeply sorry", reports broad recovery, and says it will give a fuller explanation in a full incident report. Downdetector data showed services hit in 74 countries and territories.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Oil ends a second losing week; IEA sees a surplus
item.description: 13 Nov 2026 · Brent settles 2 cents higher at $95.84 a barrel after swinging in a $2 range, its second weekly fall in a row. The International Energy Agency (IEA), which advises rich countries on energy, says the oil market will be in surplus this quarter for the first time since the war began, as high prices have cut demand. Iran said four tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz the day before.

item.title: Rupee: Slips to 94.20 on US rate worries
item.description: 13 Nov 2026 · The rupee falls 8 paise to close at 94.20 per dollar (provisional). Dealers point to a stronger dollar after higher-than-expected US inflation data, which raised bets that the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December, and to falling Indian shares.

item.title: SpiceJet: Nine of 12 planes flying; staff say salaries are late
item.description: 12 Nov · Mint reports that only nine of SpiceJet's 12 aircraft are flying, with three grounded because the airline is struggling to pay lessors. Two employees tell Mint that salaries are delayed, some by more than four months; Mint says it could not verify this. SpiceJet has not commented.

item.title: SpiceJet: Dubai flights cancelled over unpaid dues
item.description: 12 Nov (Thursday) · Reports say SpiceJet passengers in Dubai were refused check-in over unpaid dues, reported at ₹36 crore, and four SpiceJet flights from Dubai were cancelled. SpiceJet says it has "adequate bank guarantee cover in place" and is in talks with Dubai authorities.

item.title: AI this week: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen
item.description: 12 Nov 2026 · Google's new fast, cheaper model replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash and is rolling out in Search for all users, in the Gemini app and to developers.

item.title: AI model tracker: Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
item.description: 12 Nov 2026 · Google's fast everyday model, replacing Gemini 3.8 Flash; in Search, the Gemini app and the API.

item.title: Google Gemini: Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the new everyday model
item.description: 12 Nov 2026 · Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, cheaper model built for AI agents that replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash as its everyday model. It is rolling out globally in Google Search for all users, in the Gemini app (free users get it through automatic model selection) and to developers at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google says it finishes tasks 2.5 times faster than 3.8 Flash; these are Google's own figures.
